newsitem.title: USA: Niagara Mohawk seeks rate case extension.
newsitem.headline: Niagara Mohawk seeks rate case extension.

text.p: Niagara Mohawk Power Corp and the New York Department of Public Service staff have jointly asked to extend by another 30 days Niagara Mohawk's 1997 rate request proceedings so parties can continue to focus on issues related to the company's PowerChoice proposal, the utility said Tuesday.
Four previous extensions in the case have been granted.
If granted, the newest extension would change the effective date of Niagara Mohawk's requested rate increase to August 8, 1997, the company said.

In a letter to PSC Administrative Law Judge William Bouteiller, the company and PSC staff said, as with the other extensions, this latest request would, "allow the parties participating in various aspects of the PowerChoice negotiations additional time to pursue a viable long-term solution to the issues facing Niagara Mohawk."
Such a solution might eliminate the need for the rate case, the letter noted.
Spokeswoman Kerry P. Burns said the major negotiations focus on the utility's contracts with independent, non-utility power producers.
Those with investments in the independent producers say the talks are making progress.
PowerChoice, filed October 1995, is Niagara Mohawk's proposal to create a competitive electricity market, allow customers to choose their electricity supplier and restructure Niagara Mohawk.

In February, the company filed an 8.4 percent average rate increase to become effective January 1, 1997, due in part to the rising cost of power it must continue to buy from Independent Power Producers if PowerChoice is not achieved. This date has now been delayed until August.
